**Title:** Same Name, Different Unit: Identifying Source-Specific Units in Web Price Fusion

**Abstract (295 words):**

Web services that fuse values from many sources, such as price aggregators, indexes and oracles, assume that sources with the same unit name share one backing. Often they do not: a platform's ledger balance can carry the name of a common unit, the dollar, without its backing, and fusion reads a shift in that backing as a change in value. We model each source's values as true values plus a source-unit offset shared by all its items. Agreement across unrelated items identifies the offset, and a unit anchor, an item fixed in the true unit, separates a unit shift from demand. We formalise the test with an identification result, a GMM over-identification test and a simulation of size and power. On cryptocurrency exchanges, whose dollars are ledger claims, it tests a reading that Flowerday et al. (2026) say cannot be tested directly with their data. In the anchored window from 2018-11-27 to 2019-05-31, netting Tether's external price from Kraken out of Bitfinex's USDT/USD price makes it track Bitfinex's offset with slope close to one (0.97, 95% month-block bootstrap interval 0.94 to 1.00, up from 0.71): the offset's variation was mostly a ledger-dollar shift. Binance.US's 2023 slope was near one (1.00), which is close to mechanical once deposits closed; its two-anchor test rejected. On assets withheld from development, one offset per source-hour removed 0.989 of the mean-square gap from 2017 to 2019 and 0.353 from 2020 to 2023 (pooled; median over assets 0.378). Across three locked fusion tests a plain median was hard to beat; unit-aware fusion won once (USDC 2023, error 0.72 of the median's). In a pre-registered follow-up on untouched events (three USDT events) where most volume shared a stablecoin unit that moved, a frozen unit-aware fuser beat the median, unit conversion and CRH.

**Suggested keywords:** exchange dollars; unit of account; truth discovery; price feeds and oracles; Web data quality; cryptocurrency markets; reproducibility
